target_customer: Personal injury and plaintiff law firms, medical-legal service providers and claims organizations (originally physicians, attorneys and insurance claims teams)
problem: Retrieving, indexing and summarizing patient medical records for legal and claims cases is slow and manual. InQuery automates record review and now also retrieves records.
business_model: Service plus software per case or per page (pricing not verified)
product_category: Legal tech and health records AI

founders.name: Erick Enriquez
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Stanford CS and DoorDash Data Infrastructure.

founders.name: Khalil Miri
founders.background_notes: YC page header says Founder/CPO but bio says Cofounder and CTO; former quant trader and Math Olympiad medalist. Founders met as freshman dorm roommates.

competitors.name: Wisedocs
competitors.what: ML SaaS for medical record review, indexing and summarization for carriers, law firms and TPAs
competitors.funding_then: 9.5M USD Series A in Feb 2024 after 4.1M USD seed in 2022

technical_complexity.rationale: Ingesting messy scanned records, labeling and LLM summarization with HIPAA and SOC 2 controls is moderate engineering with hard accuracy requirements.

defensibility.rationale: Several record-review vendors existed and large legal AI players could add it. Integrations with Filevine and Clio and compliance certification add mild stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: EvenUp raised 135M USD in Oct 2024 and Supio launched with a 25M USD Series A in Aug 2024 per a third party profile, both covering medical records. No acquisition of InQuery found.

market_need_then: Personal injury firms and carriers spend heavy staff time on medical chronologies, evidenced by funding of Wisedocs in early 2024.

branding.domain_note: Uses inquery.ai; YC slug inquery-2 suggests the plain name was already taken in YC.

identity.visual_style: B2B legal tech site with testimonials
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and plain, for example 'We get the medical records, so your team can work the case'

brand_strength.rationale: A functional, search-confusable name with no sourced press about the brand.

pivots.from: Automated medical record review and summaries for physicians, attorneys and claims teams
pivots.to: Medical records retrieval and chronologies for personal injury law firms
pivots.why: Not stated; the shift is visible from the YC launch description versus the current site. Date unknown.

outcome_analysis: InQuery is active and has narrowed from generic medical record summarization toward records retrieval for personal injury firms, claiming over 1M pages processed. It faces heavily funded legal AI rivals that cover similar workflows. Funding amounts are inconsistent across aggregators, so scale of traction and runway cannot be judged.
notes: Amounts unverified and conflicting: Caplight seed Apr 2024 with 2.5M total, VCBacked and Foundernest 500K pre-seed Apr 2024, geo.sig.ai 3.1M. The company homepage confirms investors only, so the round is recorded with null amount and stage other. Location conflicts between NYC and San Francisco across aggregators; YC says NYC. Competitor entry is the one dated source found near the W24 batch; later entrants noted in takeover outcome only.
